items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro (Highspeed) now available on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary:
Today, Kimi K3.1 Pro from Moonshot AI is available on Amazon Bedrock, expanding our open weight model portfolio with the security and governance that customers rely on. Customers using Amazon Bedrock can now run agentic use cases such as coding and document processing on Kimi K3.1 Pro (Highspeed), which delivers high output tokens per second (OTPS) for faster, more responsive results.

According to Moonshot AI, Kimi K3.1 Pro is an open-weight, natively multimodal agentic model with a 1-million-token context window, and its most capable 3-trillion-parameter-class model to date. Moonshot AI reports improvements in coding, 3D creation, financial research, and other agentic work. On Amazon Bedrock, it runs within the same security boundary as proprietary models and supports explicit prompt caching to reduce latency and input costs.

Kimi K3.1 Pro is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock is available through cross-Region inference. To get started, visit the Amazon Bedrock console. To learn more, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation.

items.title: Agent Registry is now generally available in AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region
items.summary:
AWS Agent Registry, available through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, is now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region.

AWS Agent Registry is a fully managed discovery service that gives your organization a central catalog for organizing, curating, and discovering resources. You can publish MCP servers, tools, agents, agent skills, and custom resources to a searchable registry, and control what becomes discoverable through an approval workflow. People and AI agents can then find the right tools and agents through hybrid search, catalog browsing, and a native MCP endpoint.

With Agent Registry in AWS GovCloud (US-West), public sector organizations and their partners get a single governed inventory of the agents and tools in their environment. Approval workflows and AWS CloudTrail audit logs support their compliance and oversight requirements.

To get started, see the AWS Agent Registry documentation.

items.title: Amazon MSK Replicator is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East, US-West) Regions
items.summary:
You can now use Amazon MSK Replicator in the AWS GovCloud (US-East, US-West) Regions to replicate streaming data across Amazon MSK clusters and from external Apache Kafka clusters including on-premises, self-managed on AWS, or other cloud providers to Amazon MSK Provisioned clusters.

MSK Replicator is a feature of Amazon MSK that automates data replication between Kafka clusters, eliminating the need to manage custom replication infrastructure or configure open-source tools. With MSK Replicator, you can easily build regionally resilient streaming applications for increased availability and business continuity. MSK Replicator provides automatic asynchronous replication across Kafka clusters, eliminating the need to write custom code, manage infrastructure, or setup cross-region networking. MSK Replicator automatically scales the underlying resources so that you can replicate data on-demand without having to monitor or scale capacity. MSK Replicator also replicates the necessary Kafka metadata including topic configurations, Access Control Lists (ACLs), and consumer group offsets. If an unexpected event occurs in a region, you can failover to the other AWS Region and seamlessly resume processing.

You can get started with MSK Replicator from the Amazon MSK console or the Amazon CLI. To learn more, visit the MSK Replicator documentation, product page, and pricing page.

items.title: Amazon Redshift expands SUPER data type to store strings up to 16 million bytes
items.summary:
Amazon Redshift now supports individual strings up to 16 million bytes within SUPER data types. Once you opt in through a database parameter, this enhancement applies when ingesting structured or semi-structured data from JSON, PARQUET, TEXT, and CSV source files, and when transforming data through extract load and transform (ELT) processes. Previously, individual strings within SUPER data types were limited to 65,535 bytes.

Storing large individual strings in the SUPER data type helps avoid complex pre-loading transformations needed to store the source data in Amazon Redshift. You can now directly ingest large individual strings greater than 65,535 bytes without extra processing (for example, lengthy documents like terms and conditions and contracts), making them queryable using SQL. Once the data is in Amazon Redshift, you can use the flexibility of PartiQL language to explore and navigate through the data or use string functions to transform the data. Functions such as JSON_PARSE, CONCAT, and LISTAGG can now take input strings and return output strings up to 16 million bytes in length.

This enhancement is available in all AWS Regions, including the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, where Amazon Redshift is available. See the AWS Region Table for more details. To learn more, please visit our documentation or blog.

items.title: AWS launches support for amortization of EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML
items.summary:
AWS Data Exports for Cost and Usage Report (CUR) 2.0 and AWS Cost Explorer now amortize the upfront fee for Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML across the duration of each reservation. You can see the amortized cost of each instance launched into a Capacity Block and the amortized cost of unused capacity, so you can attribute your upfront fee to the workloads that used it and identify capacity that went unused.

Previously, a Capacity Block's upfront fee appeared as a single charge on the purchase date, making it difficult to see how that cost was spread across usage over the reservation. Now the amortized cost appears alongside your instance usage, so you can allocate GPU costs to the teams, projects, and applications that ran on the reserved capacity. You can also see what share of your reservation went unused and plan future Capacity Block purchases. In CUR 2.0, the amortized costs appear in the reservation_amortized_upfront_fee_for_billing_period, reservation_effective_cost columns, and reservation_net_effective_cost shows the amortized cost after discounts. In Cost Explorer, select the amortized cost view to see Capacity Block costs allocated for the reservation.

 Amortization for Capacity Blocks is available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions except the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions and the China Regions. To learn more, see the CUR 2.0 data dictionary and exploring your data using Cost Explorer.

items.title: Capacity Reservation Resource Groups now support Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks and interruptible Capacity Reservations in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
items.summary:
Starting today, you can add Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML and interruptible Capacity Reservations to Capacity Reservation Resource Groups in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. Amazon EC2 offers different reservation offerings such as On-Demand Capacity Reservations (ODCRs), interruptible Capacity Reservations, and Capacity Blocks for ML. Previously, a Capacity Reservation Resource Group could only include ODCRs. Now you can add any type of Capacity Reservation to a Capacity Reservation Resource Group, making it easier to launch EC2 instances across your entire portfolio of reserved capacity.

To use this feature, create a Capacity Reservation Resource Group, add any Capacity Reservation to it, and then target the group in your launch request. When using EC2 Fleet and EC2 Auto Scaling groups, you can also specify your prioritization preferences across reservation types, and configure automatic fall back to EC2 On-Demand capacity when there is no capacity remaining across your reservations.

There are no additional charges for using this feature. With the addition of AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, this feature is now available in all AWS Regions where Capacity Blocks for ML and interruptible ODCRs are supported, excluding China Regions. To get started, see Capacity Reservation Resource Groups and the Capacity Reservations user guide.

items.title: Amazon Simple Email Service is now available in six new AWS Regions
items.summary:
Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES)  is now available in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand, Melbourne, Taipei, Thailand), Mexico (Central), EU (Spain). Customers can now use these new Regions to leverage Amazon SES to send emails and, if needed, to help manage data requirements.

Amazon SES is a scalable, cost-effective, and flexible cloud-based email service that allows digital marketers and application developers to send marketing, notification, and transactional emails from within any application. To learn more about Amazon SES, visit this page .

With this launch, Amazon SES is available in 35 AWS Regions globally: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (N. California, Oregon), AWS GovCloud (US-West, US-East), Asia Pacific (Osaka, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Sydney, Singapore, Seoul, Tokyo, Jakarta, Malaysia, New Zealand, Melbourne, Taipei, Thailand), Canada (Central, Calgary), EU (Ireland, Frankfurt, London, Paris, Stockholm, Milan, Zurich,Spain), Middle East (Bahrain, UAE), Israel (Tel Aviv), South America (Sao Paulo), Mexico (Central) and Africa (Cape Town).

For a complete list of all of the regional endpoints for Amazon SES, see  AWS Service Endpoints  in the AWS General Reference.

items.title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports catalog-vended credentials with Apache Iceberg REST catalog federation
items.summary:
AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports external catalog's vended credentials in Apache Iceberg REST catalog federation. You can now read external Iceberg tables from Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, Amazon Redshift, and AWS Glue using coarse-grained table grants in your external Iceberg catalog.

Glue Data Catalog already federates to external Iceberg REST catalogs through an AWS IAM role that you configure with access to your Amazon S3 buckets. This enhancement in Glue Data Catalog provides another way to connect to an external Iceberg catalog and read only the tables that the external catalog authorizes. It uses temporary security credentials that are scoped to the Amazon S3 storage prefix and vended by your external Iceberg catalog. AWS Lake Formation manages access control when you query an external table using any AWS analytics engine, letting you restrict access further down to specific rows and columns and share external Iceberg tables across AWS accounts.

This feature is available through the AWS Lake Formation Management Console, AWS CLI, and the AWS Glue and Lake Formation SDKs. This feature is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Glue and Lake Formation are supported. To learn more, visit the documentation.

items.title: AWS Elemental MediaConvert adds a native integration with AWS Elemental Inference Smart Subtitles
items.summary:
​​AWS Elemental MediaConvert now integrates Smart Subtitles, an AI-powered subtitling solution built on AWS Elemental Inference and the latest speech recognition models. This feature brings automated subtitle generation directly into your video-on-demand (VOD) transcoding and packaging workflows, eliminating the need for separate external captioning pipelines. Customers can now manage both transcoding and subtitle creation within a single, unified workflow.

​Smart subtitles automatically transcribe your audio into subtitles with native support for six languages including English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish. With MediaConvert, you can package the outputs to text-based side-car formats and burn-in for all your streaming or distribution needs. To enhance transcription quality, you can now define custom dictionaries in Elemental Inference to guide the model on proper nouns, brand names, technical terminology, and more. Smart subtitles complement existing add-on features such as Smart Cropping for end-to-end media pipelines, intelligent framing and accessible subtitle delivery in distribution-ready formats like HLS and DASH.​

​​Smart subtitles is available in all AWS regions where Elemental Inference is available including US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), and Asia Pacific (Sydney).​

To learn more, visit Smart subtitles with MediaConvert, AWS Elemental MediaConvert  and AWS Elemental Inference smart subtitles.

items.title: AWS Security Hub now provides an SBOM inventory for your compute resources
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces that AWS Security Hub now provides a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) inventory, giving central security teams a continuously updated, organization-wide view of the software packages and applications installed on their compute resources.

Security Hub builds the inventory from the SBOMs that Amazon Inspector generates for Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon ECR container images, and AWS Lambda functions, with no additional configuration. The SBOM page lists each package with its version, type, and the number of resources where it is installed. You can filter and group the list by package attributes, account, and region. On the resource detail page, the Installed software tab lists every package on that resource, so you can judge its function and criticality while triaging any finding. You can also query the inventory through the Security Hub API.

The SBOM inventory is included with Security Hub Essentials at no additional cost. It requires no new enablement and populates automatically where Amazon Inspector is enabled. It is available in all AWS Regions where Security Hub is available. To learn more, see the AWS Security Hub User Guide and the AWS Security Hub product page.

items.title: AWS Interconnect - last mile announces new metro in Northern Virginia, USA
items.summary:
Today, AWS announced a new AWS Interconnect - last mile metro in Northern Virginia, USA. Northern Virginia joins New York as the second metro where you can connect your data center, branch office, or colocation facility to AWS. 

AWS Interconnect - last mile gives you managed, private, resilient connections to AWS, so you don't have to order cross-connects or configure routers. Every connection is provisioned by default across two physically diverse locations with four redundant links, providing maximum resilience out of the box and backed by a 99.99% availability SLA up to the Direct Connect port. Traffic between AWS and partner edge devices is encrypted with MACsec by default.

Lumen customers anywhere in the continental United States can order generally available connections through the Northern Virginia metro to reach all public AWS Regions (except those in China) and AWS Local Zones. AWS Interconnect - last mile is also available in preview through Megaport and Equinix in the Northern Virginia metro. You can create connections using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS Interconnect API. For pricing, see AWS Interconnect - last mile pricing.

items.title: Announcing Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary:
Today, we are announcing the general availability of Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Web Answer is a managed tool that returns a synthesized, grounded, cited answer to a natural-language question in a single call, so agent builders can attach it to an agent and get back a finished answer grounded in current web sources, without building and maintaining their own search, retrieve, synthesis, and citation pipeline. 

Web Answer builds on Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which launched in June, extending it from "find the web content" to "return the finished answer," a capability customers have been asking for. With Web Answer, your agent sends a question and receives a synthesized cited answer in one tool call. Web Answer works like an agent; it plans its own searches, runs several in parallel, and decides when it has gathered enough evidence to answer. You stay in control of the boundaries, with domain include, deny lists and publish-date filters that scope where it looks. It attaches as a target on an AgentCore Gateway and is called over MCP, authenticated with IAM, with zero data egress. 

Web Answer is available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region, with per-tool call pricing. 

To learn more about Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, see Web Answer’s documentation page and Web Answer’s website. For Region availability, see the AWS Region table.

items.title: AWS Network Load Balancer is now available in the AWS Phoenix Local Zone
items.summary:
AWS Network Load Balancer is now available in the Phoenix Local Zone (us-west-2-phx-2a). AWS Local Zones is a type of AWS infrastructure deployment that places AWS compute, storage, database, and other select services closer to large population, industry, and IT centers where no AWS Region exists today.

With this launch, you can create an AWS Network Load Balancer directly in the Phoenix Local Zone. Previously, if your targets ran in the Phoenix Local Zone, you had to place the load balancer in an Availability Zone in the parent Region, so connections and their traffic had to travel to the parent Region and back. This added latency and routed traffic outside the zone where your application runs. Now, connection routing stays local to your targets, delivering lower and more consistent latency to end users in the Phoenix metro area and keeping traffic within the Local Zone. This is especially valuable for latency-sensitive workloads such as real-time gaming, media streaming, and live financial applications serving users in the region.

To learn more about Network Load Balancer, visit the documentation. For more information on AWS Local Zones, visit the AWS Local Zones website. The Locations webpage lists the available and announced Local Zones. You can enable AWS Local Zones from the Local Zones tab in the AWS Global View console, or the ModifyAvailabilityZoneGroup API.

items.title: Amazon DynamoDB now supports bulk put items
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces the general availability of bulk put items for Amazon DynamoDB, a fully managed feature that writes data from Amazon S3 into your existing DynamoDB tables. Many DynamoDB applications use data that other systems produce and store in Amazon S3. Writing this data into existing DynamoDB tables has typically meant building custom pipelines and managing table capacity. With bulk put items, developers and data engineers can write this data without impacting existing workloads or building a custom ingestion pipeline, in a cost-efficient way.

You point bulk put items at the S3 location of your input files, and DynamoDB handles the rest. Each item supports its own condition expression, so you can enforce insert-only or version-guarded writes. The Standard tier fits most workloads, and the Accelerated tier is for more time-sensitive workloads. Common use cases include daily refreshes, large catalog enrichments, backfills, and migrations.

Bulk put items with Standard tier is available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, to see the list where the Accelerated tier is available see the regional availability. To learn more, visit the Introducing bulk put items for Amazon DynamoDB blog and the Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon Cognito announces 99.99% Service Level Agreement for the Plus feature plan
items.summary:
Starting November 1, 2026, the Amazon Cognito Service Level Agreement (SLA) commits to a Monthly Uptime Percentage of 99.99% for user pools on the Plus feature plan, up from 99.9%. User pools already on Plus are automatically covered by the new Service Commitment. User pools on Essentials and Lite stay at the 99.9% Service Commitment with no change to their terms.

To qualify for the 99.99% Service Commitment, you can switch a user pool to the Plus feature plan using the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), or AWS Software Development Kits (SDKs). The Plus feature plan also includes threat protection features such as adaptive authentication, compromised credentials detection, and threat and user activity logging and export.

For full terms and exclusions, see the Amazon Cognito SLA. To learn more about feature plans, see user pool feature plans.

items.title: IAM Roles Anywhere now supports automatic certificate revocation checking
items.summary:
AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Roles Anywhere now supports automatic revocation checking using certificate revocation list (CRL) distribution points (CDPs). This helps keep revocation checks in sync with your certificate authority (CA) and can help improve your security posture. When you enable this capability on a trust anchor, IAM Roles Anywhere reads the CDP URLs embedded in authenticating certificates, downloads the corresponding CRLs, and denies credential requests that use revoked certificates.

Previously, to check revocation status, you had to import CRLs into IAM Roles Anywhere and re-import them each time your CA published an update, which added operational overhead. With this launch, IAM Roles Anywhere downloads CRLs from your CDPs and refreshes them periodically, so you no longer need to re-import them. You can use this capability with AWS Private Certificate Authority or your own public key infrastructure (PKI), provided your certificates include publicly accessible CDP URLs that meet the distribution point requirements. To enable it on a trust anchor, use the IAM Roles Anywhere console, AWS SDKs, or AWS CLI.

This feature is available at no additional cost in all commercial AWS Regions. To learn more, see Automatic revocation checking with CRL distribution points in the IAM Roles Anywhere User Guide.

items.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service optimized engine now supports agent traces
items.summary:
Today, the Amazon OpenSearch Service optimized engine adds support for agent traces, including OpenTelemetry traces. Your traces and logs now live in the same place. You can follow a request or an agent session from start to finish, find the step that failed or slowed down, and check the related logs without switching tools. 

The optimized engine maps OpenTelemetry logs and traces to object, nested, and flat object fields, with support for multi-valued arrays. Span events, span links, prompts, and tool calls retain their nested structure, allowing field-level queries without flattening data during ingestion.

On hot-tier data, the engine supports update, delete, and upsert operations by document ID. When data arrives late or with errors, you can correct it in place, so your dashboards and alerts work from accurate data. In OpenSearch UI, you can analyze this data with Discover Traces, application performance monitoring, the service map, and the agent traces and sessions views.

These features are available on OpenSearch 3.7, at no additional charge in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), and Europe (Spain).  To get started, send OpenTelemetry data to your domain, for example by using Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion. To learn more, see the documentation.

items.title: Amazon FSx for Lustre delivers 16x higher metadata IOPS on Intelligent-Tiering file systems
items.summary:
Amazon FSx for Lustre now supports up to 192,000 metadata I/O operations per second (IOPS) on file systems that use the Intelligent-Tiering storage class, 16x higher than the previous maximum of 12,000 IOPS.

The FSx for Lustre Intelligent-Tiering storage class delivers the lowest-cost and only fully elastic Lustre file storage in the cloud. It is optimized for workloads that mix hot and cold data and do not require consistent SSD-level performance. A file system's metadata IOPS determine how many files and directories you can create, list, read, and delete per second. Today's launch allows you to scale to even higher levels of performance, accelerate time-to-results, and optimize your storage costs for metadata-intensive machine learning research and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads.

Higher metadata IOPS are available on new FSx for Lustre Intelligent-Tiering file systems in all AWS Regions where the Intelligent-Tiering storage class is available. For more information about the file system metadata performance, see the Amazon FSx for Lustre User Guide.

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports Kerberos authentication with self-managed Active Directory
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle (Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle) now allows customers to join their RDS for Oracle DB instances directly to their self-managed Microsoft Active Directory (AD) domain. Your self-managed AD can run on premises, on Amazon EC2, or with another cloud provider. Users in your AD domain can authenticate to RDS for Oracle DB instances using Kerberos.

Previously, in order to use Kerberos authentication with self-managed AD for their RDS for Oracle instances, customers were required to deploy AWS Managed Microsoft AD and establish trust between AWS managed domain and self-managed domain. Now, customers can join their existing self-managed AD directly to authenticate and authorize users without setting up an additional directory or trust relationship. You can set this up using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDK. You can use self-managed AD without any additional charge.

Kerberos authentication with self-managed Active Directory in Amazon RDS for Oracle is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for Oracle is available. To learn more about Kerberos authentication with self-managed Active Directory, visit Working with self-managed Active Directory with an Amazon RDS for Oracle DB instance in the Amazon RDS User Guide.

items.title: AWS Security Hub Network Scanning now available in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
AWS Security Hub Network Scanning feature is now supported in AWS GovCloud (US).

Network Scanning probes your resources from the internet to detect actual reachability, not just what could be reachable based on security group rules and route tables. It discovers public IP addresses, virtual machines, and load balancers across your AWS environments, identifies reachable ports, and determines what services are running behind them. This complements Security Hub's existing network reachability findings, which identify configurations that could make a resource reachable from the internet. Network Scanning confirms that configurations do exist which make a resource reachable from the internet. Each reachable port generates a Security Hub finding with evidence of the port and service discovered. Security Hub Exposures then automatically correlates these findings with other findings and resource configurations to determine broader risk.

Existing customers can enable Network Scanning in individual accounts and regions, or across an organization via a configuration policy. For new Security Hub customers, Network Scanning is on by default. Network Scanning is included with Security Hub Essentials at no additional cost in all AWS commercial and GovCloud (US) Regions that support Security Hub. To learn more, see the AWS Security Hub User Guide and the AWS Security Hub product page. For the full list of Regions, see the AWS Regional Services List.

items.title: AWS Lambda durable functions increases default execution and API quotas
items.summary:
AWS Lambda durable functions has increased default quotas for running executions and API request rates. The new quotas below apply in all AWS Regions except US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Europe (Ireland), which have twice these quotas.

  • Running durable executions per account (1 million to 5 million)
  • Function invocation rate to start durable executions (300 to 3,000 requests per second)
  • CheckpointDurableExecution and GetDurableExecutionState (1,000 to 10,000 requests per second)
  • SendDurableExecutionCallbackSuccess, SendDurableExecutionCallbackFailure, and SendDurableExecutionCallbackHeartbeat (300 to 3,000 requests per second)
  • GetDurableExecution and StopDurableExecution (30 to 300 requests per second)
  • GetDurableExecutionHistory and ListDurableExecutionsByFunction (15 to 150 requests per second)

AWS Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that execute for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing, automatic retries, and waits that suspend execution without incurring compute charges. With this increase, workloads such as order processing and document pipelines can run more executions in parallel without requesting quota increases. When many executions wait on external work, such as payment confirmations or batch jobs, more can resume together. If you monitor and manage executions with your dashboards or scripts, they can now check status, list executions, read history, and stop executions at least ten times as often.

The new quotas apply in all AWS Regions where AWS Lambda durable functions is available. To learn more, see Lambda quotas in the AWS Lambda Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon EC2 now publishes ImdsV1Enabled CloudWatch metric
items.summary:
Amazon EC2 now supports an ImdsV1Enabled CloudWatch metric, giving customers visibility into which of their EC2 instances still have Instance Metadata Service Version 1 (IMDSv1) enabled. You can use this metric to track your migration to IMDSv2 across your accounts and Regions, at scale.

With the ImdsV1Enabled metric, you can configure CloudWatch dashboards and alarms to track instances that still allow IMDSv1, identify migration gaps, and prioritize remediation, without building your own tooling to check the metadata options of instances across accounts and Regions. This gives you a reliable, ongoing signal to track and complete your IMDSv2 migration.

The ImdsV1Enabled CloudWatch metric is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost.

To learn more, see the ImdsV1Enabled CloudWatch metric in the Amazon EC2 User Guide. For step-by-step migration instructions, see Transition to IMDSv2 in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

items.title: AWS CodeConnections is now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region
items.summary:
AWS CodeConnections is now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region, in addition to AWS GovCloud (US-East). CodeConnections lets you connect AWS services such as AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild to source code repositories hosted with third-party providers such as Bitbucket.

With this launch, customers running workloads in AWS GovCloud (US-West) can create connections to their source repositories in the same Region as their pipelines. For example, a team can configure a connection so that a commit to their repository automatically starts a release in AWS CodePipeline, without managing provider credentials for each integration.

To learn more, see the AWS CodeConnections User Guide and the AWS GovCloud User Guide. To get started, visit the AWS GovCloud (US) console.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI Studio Now Supports IAM Identity Center Multi-Region Replication
items.summary:
Amazon SageMaker AI now supports IAM Identity Center (IdC) multi-region replication, enabling you to deploy SageMaker AI Studio domains in different regions from your IdC instance's primary region. Previously, the primary IdC instance had to reside in the same region as the SageMaker AI Studio domain; now customers can replicate their primary IdC instance into the region where they wish to use SageMaker AI Studio domains. This capability helps customers maintain compliance while utilizing centralized workforce identity management.

As an Amazon SageMaker AI Studio administrator, you can deploy SageMaker AI domains that align with your workforce's location and data residency requirements, independent of where your primary IdC instance is set up. Organizations can retain their primary IdC instance in one region while operating SageMaker AI Studio workloads in compliance-mandated regions, support global operations through centralized identity management, and satisfy data sovereignty requirements without compromising single sign-on (SSO) capabilities.

To get started see the SageMaker AI documentation and to learn about setting up IAM Identity Center multi-region support see the IAM Identity Center User Guide.

Multi-region IdC replication is available in all standard AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker AI Studio is supported, including: Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Ireland), US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), South America (São Paulo), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Europe (Paris), Europe (Stockholm).

items.title: AWS WAF AI traffic monetization now supports fiat payouts through Stripe
items.summary:
AWS WAF AI traffic monetization now integrates with Stripe. Publishers, content owners, and API providers can collect stablecoin payments from AI bots and agents that settle in local currency directly to their Stripe balance. With this launch, customers can monetize agent access without holding stablecoins or managing a crypto wallet. Stripe is now available as a new payout method alongside existing stablecoin payouts.

To get started, connect your Stripe account to AWS WAF through Stripe Connect in the AWS WAF console. Your existing pricing and agent policies work unchanged. When an agent requests protected content, AWS WAF returns an HTTP 402 response with the valid payment credential types that it accepts. Once the agent returns with a valid payment credential and makes the request again, the content is returned ungated. Revenue from all payment providers appears in the AWS WAF console revenue analytics.

The Stripe integration is available at no additional charge to all AWS WAF customers using Amazon CloudFront, in all edge locations where AWS WAF web ACLs are associated with CloudFront distributions. Standard AWS WAF and Stripe processing fees apply. See AWS WAF pricing for details.

To get started, visit the AWS WAF console or explore the AWS WAF Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon Q Developer in console is now the AWS assistant
items.summary:
Amazon Q Developer in the AWS Management Console and Console Mobile Apps is now called the AWS assistant. Previously, customers interacted with Amazon Q Developer across these surfaces. Now, the AWS assistant provides the same personalized, account-aware guidance and actions with a name that immediately communicates what the product does.

The AWS assistant simplifies how customers build, operate, and optimize on AWS. The AWS assistant is currently offered for free. Existing Amazon Q Developer Pro subscribers will automatically retain their Pro Tier capabilities under the AWS assistant.

The AWS assistant is available globally. To learn more, visit aws.amazon.com/products/assistant/.

items.title: ﻿﻿AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store now allows organization and validation with built-in data types
items.summary:
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store now supports 13 new parameter data types that automatically validate parameter values when you create or update a parameter. With built-in validation, you can stop malformed configuration values, such as an invalid IP address, AWS account ID, or JSON document, before your applications read them, without writing your own validation logic. These types allow you to better organize your parameters across your workloads. You can filter by type when calling the DescribeParameters API or when browsing parameters in the Parameter Store console.

The following data types are available for both standard and advanced parameters:  aws:region, aws:account:id, boolean, integer, float, binary, hostname, email, ipv4-address, and ipv6-address. Three more data types, url, json, and jsonc, are available for advanced parameters. Parameter Store checks the value when you call PutParameter and rejects any value that doesn't match its data type. New data types work with String and SecureString parameters, and several also support StringList parameters, where each item in the list is validated. You can combine a data type with an AllowedPattern for additional constraints, and you can change the data type of an existing text parameter.

items.title: Amazon MWAA now supports cost allocation tags
items.summary:
Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA) now supports cost allocation tags. Tags you apply to an Amazon MWAA environment now propagate to the compute that runs it, including workers, schedulers, and web servers. You can then track Amazon MWAA spend by tag in AWS Cost Explorer and AWS Cost and Usage Reports.

With this launch, platform teams can show back or charge back Airflow costs to the team, project, or cost center that owns each environment. You can use cost allocation tags when you create a new environment or update an existing one. To get started, tag your environment using the Amazon MWAA console, AWS CLI, or Amazon MWAA API, then activate the tag key as a cost allocation tag in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon MWAA is available. For more information, see the AWS Region table. To learn more, visit Cost allocation tags in Amazon MWAA in the Amazon MWAA User Guide.

items.title: Amazon ECS Managed Daemons can now collect json-file logs from application containers on Amazon ECS Managed Instances
items.summary:
Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) introduces json-file log driver support for Amazon ECS Managed Instances and log driver volumes for Amazon ECS Managed Daemons. Together, these features let you collect application logs with the observability agent of your choice and forward them to any destination you choose.

With this launch, your application containers on ECS Managed Instances can write their logs as local files in standard Docker json-file format, which most observability agents read natively. Your managed daemons can directly read these files through a volume mount, without specifying host bind mount paths or requiring root privileges. As a result, one managed daemon on each instance can collect logs from every application container that uses the json-file log driver. Amazon ECS keeps each container's logs in a dedicated directory named with the container ID and retains them until the container is removed, so your managed daemon can use native file-based log collection and trace every log back to the container that produced it.

To get started, set the log driver to json-file in the logConfiguration of your application task definition. Next, register a daemon task definition that specifies a volume with logDriverVolumeConfiguration, and mount the volume into your daemon container using mountPoints. You can configure this using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, API, AWS SDKs or AWS CloudFormation. This feature is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon ECS Managed Instances and Managed Daemons are available, at no additional cost. To learn more, refer to our documentation page and visit Amazon ECS Managed Instances.

items.title: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is now available in the Asia Pacific (Taipei) and Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Regions
items.summary:
Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is now available in the Asia Pacific (Taipei) and Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Regions, adding to the list of available Regions where you can use Amazon DocumentDB.

Amazon DocumentDB is a fully managed, native JSON database that makes it simple and cost-effective to operate critical document workloads at virtually any scale without managing infrastructure. Amazon DocumentDB is designed to give you the scalability and durability you need when operating mission-critical MongoDB workloads. Storage scales automatically up to 128 TiB without any impact to your application. In addition, Amazon DocumentDB natively integrates with Amazon CloudWatch, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Lambda, AWS Backup, and more. Amazon DocumentDB supports millions of requests per second and can be scaled out to 15 low-latency read replicas in minutes with no application downtime.

To learn more about Amazon DocumentDB, please visit the Amazon DocumentDB product page and pricing page. You can create an Amazon DocumentDB cluster from the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), or AWS SDKs.

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports copying option groups during cross-Region snapshot copy
items.summary:
Amazon RDS for Oracle now lets you copy the option group associated with a DB snapshot when you copy that snapshot to another AWS Region.

Amazon RDS for Oracle uses option groups to enable and configure features that make it simple to manage your databases. Option groups are specific to the AWS Region where you create them. Previously, customers wanting to replicate RDS backups that had option groups to a different AWS Region had to copy the snapshot without the option group and then recreate the option group in the target Region before restoring the snapshot. Now, you no longer need to separate the steps and can instead initiate the snapshot copy and specify the option group copy in the same request as the snapshot copy.

The existing boolean parameter CopyOptionGroup on the CopyDBSnapshot API and CLI commands now also support cross-Region copy, along with cross-account copy. You can now copy options groups to the destination snapshot in the target AWS Region from the source snapshot by setting this parameter to true.

This capability is available on Amazon RDS for Oracle in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, review the Amazon RDS API Documentation.

items.title: AWS announces AWS Interconnect - last mile preview with Equinix
items.summary:
AWS Interconnect - last mile is now available in preview with Equinix. You can connect your infrastructure across Equinix's global network of 282 data centers worldwide to AWS in a few clicks.

Interconnect - last mile gives you managed, private, and resilient connections to AWS, so you don't have to order cross-connects or configure routers. To set up in the AWS Management Console, choose an AWS Region, a bandwidth speed, a Direct Connect gateway, and your Equinix Fabric One project ID. AWS generates an activation key, which you enter in the Equinix Fabric One portal to complete the setup. You can also initiate the connection from the Equinix Fabric One portal. AWS and Equinix set up quad-redundant capacity in advance, across two locations and four separate links, with BGP peering, VLANs and ASNs configured for you. Every connection is built for maximum resilience and comes with a 99.99% availability SLA. Traffic between AWS and Equinix edge devices is encrypted with MACsec by default.

During the preview, you can order 1 Gbps Interconnect - last mile connections at no charge to the US West (N. California) Region through the San Jose metro and to the US East (N. Virginia) Region through the Northern Virginia metro. When Interconnect - last mile with Equinix becomes generally available, you'll be able to scale bandwidth from 1 Gbps to 100 Gbps in the console. You can create connections using the console, the AWS CLI, or the API. Partners can integrate using the open API package on GitHub. To learn more, see the AWS Interconnect - last mile documentation.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer now shows associated cases in contact records
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer now includes case IDs and reference numbers in contact records, helping supervisors and analysts understand which customer issues drive contact volume. Cases track issues, such as refund requests or billing disputes, across interactions and teams. Supervisors can now identify the cases associated with an interaction directly on the Contact Details page without searching individual cases. Analysts can access the same information through the DescribeContact API and contact event streams to measure the number of interactions per case.

Cases is available in the following AWS regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation.

items.title: Amazon EC2 and VPC now display related resources for all resource types
items.summary:
Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2), Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC), and AWS Global View now display related resources for all resource types in their consoles. Previously, only security groups had an option to view related resources. Now you can see relationships for all EC2 and VPC resource types, including EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes, Launch Templates, Auto Scaling groups, subnets, route tables, and more. The Related Resources tab has also been moved to the console toolbar for easier access.

This capability helps you better understand your infrastructure dependencies and troubleshoot issues more efficiently. For example, when investigating an EC2 instance issue, you can quickly view its associated EBS volumes, security groups, subnets, and route tables without navigating between multiple console pages. Network administrators can now trace connections from a subnet to its associated route tables, network ACLs, and instances, streamlining network configuration reviews and security audits.

This feature is now available in all commercial AWS Regions.

To learn more, visit Amazon EC2 and Amazon VPC in the AWS Management Console.

items.title: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode supports OpenID Connect (OIDC) for Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure
items.summary:
AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication for Google Cloud Storage and Microsoft Azure Blob Storage locations. DataSync uses an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role to get short-lived credentials from Google Cloud or Microsoft Entra ID and refreshes them automatically so your transfers run without interruption.

You can now use DataSync to access your Google Cloud Storage and Azure Blob Storage without long-term credentials such as hash-based message authentication code (HMAC) keys or shared access signature (SAS) tokens. This lets you move data across clouds while complying with security policies that might prohibit long-term credentials.

You can get started by adding an IAM role to your DataSync location with the AWS CLI, API, or AWS CloudFormation. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where DataSync Enhanced mode is supported. To learn more, visit the AWS DataSync User Guide.

items.title: Amazon S3 Tables now provide a simple, cost-effective path for data lake modernization
items.summary:
Amazon S3 Tables now offer managed migration of your Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg. Iceberg adds ACID transactions, schema evolution, and time travel to your data lake, but moving off Hive usually means building a migration pipeline for each table, which can take weeks. You can now let S3 Tables manage your migration, resulting in query-ready Iceberg tables that stay optimized as data grows.

S3 Tables validate, convert, and copy your data while production workloads keep running. To lower migration risk, you can review each step, sync destination tables with source changes as often as you need, or roll back to your source data. You pay only for the data that the job copies, with no charge for the Hive-to-Iceberg conversion, and source objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering stay in their current access tier. If your tables use Snappy compression, S3 Tables recompress them to Zstandard (ZSTD) and compact them, which reduces storage and object count and improves query performance.

To get started, visit the AWS Management Console or use the Amazon S3 Tables migration APIs. A migration skill is also available in the Agent Toolkit for AWS to help AI agents orchestrate the workflow autonomously. At launch, S3 Tables managed migration supports AWS Glue-registered Hive tables stored in Parquet format within the same AWS account and AWS Region. It is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, Stockholm). For pricing information visit Amazon S3 pricing. To learn more, see the Amazon S3 Tables overview page, documentation, and AWS News Blog.

items.title: RHEL 10, Rocky 10 and Ubuntu 26.04 Bundles for WorkSpaces
items.summary:
AWS announces new Linux bundles for Amazon WorkSpaces Personal, including Rocky Linux 10, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. With these bundles, you can launch WorkSpaces on the latest enterprise Linux operating systems and use newer software packages that are only available in these releases. These new bundles feature modern Wayland display technology, giving you access to the latest Linux desktop capabilities. The new OS options also bring stronger security and longer support lifecycles from each distribution.

While Rocky Linux 8 and 9, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9, and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and 24.04 LTS powered WorkSpaces bundles remain available, the new bundles let you adopt the latest releases on your own timeline. Your existing WorkSpaces keep running with no changes. You can move users to the new operating systems once your applications and workflows are ready.

To get started, select a managed Rocky Linux 10, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, or Ubuntu 26.04 LTS bundle when you create a new Linux WorkSpace. These bundles are available in Standard, Performance, Power, and PowerPro sizes in all AWS Regions where Amazon WorkSpaces is available. For a full list of supported operating systems, see Bundles and images for WorkSpaces Personal. For pricing information, visit the Amazon WorkSpaces pricing page.

items.title: New features for Amazon EC2 Capacity Manager
items.summary:
Amazon EC2 Capacity Manager now offers real-time supportability checks and capacity fulfillment metrics. Real-time supportability checks help customers find capacity by scoring how well each instance type and Availability Zone can support a request, without launching or reserving instances. Capacity fulfillment metrics show how much capacity was delivered against the amount requested.

Global enterprises that run thousands of workloads across hundreds of accounts often spread each one across multiple instance types and Availability Zones, giving Amazon EC2 more options to fulfill each request. Starting today, customers can use the supportability checks in Capacity Manager to understand which Availability Zones and instance types give them the best chance of getting the capacity they need. The check returns a High, Medium, or Low score for each option, plus an overall score. Additionally, with fulfillment metrics, customers can measure fulfillment rates across their AWS organization, accounts, Regions, and tagged workloads, with a breakdown by instance type and Availability Zone, to show how well those choices are working.

Both capabilities are included with AWS Unified Operations, the AWS Support plan for global enterprises running mission-critical workloads, and are available in all commercial AWS Regions.

To learn more, read Plan and measure EC2 flexibility with Amazon EC2 Capacity Manager on the AWS Compute Blog and see the Amazon EC2 Capacity Manager user guide. To get started, visit the Capacity Manager console.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer lets agents pause and resume emails
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer lets agents pause emails while waiting for information or approvals, freeing them to handle higher-priority contacts and resume their work later. For example, an agent waiting for a supervisor to approve a refund can pause the email and take an incoming call. Paused time is tracked separately from active handling time, giving supervisors a more accurate view of the time agents spend working on emails.

Agents can pause and resume emails directly from the Agent Workspace or Contact Control Panel (CCP) and see how long each email has been paused. Supervisors can monitor paused emails and pause duration in real time, and use flows to automatically resume or transfer emails that remain paused beyond a configured threshold.

Amazon Connect Customer email pause and resume is available in the US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London) regions. To learn more and get started, please refer to the help documentation or visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.

items.title: Amazon WorkSpaces for AI agents now supports Linux and Windows 11 cloud desktops
items.summary:
WorkSpaces for AI agents now supports Linux and Windows 11 cloud desktops, in addition to Windows Server. You can run each AI agent on the operating system that its workflows and applications require. Your agents can then work in the same environments that your workforce already uses, without re-platforming. 

Linux desktops give agents full root access to the operating system where many developers already build, test, and automate agentic workflows. Agents can take on developer tasks, such as running builds, tests, and scripts, within the enterprise-grade security and governance controls you already rely on. Windows 11 desktops let agents work in the enterprise applications your teams depend on every day.

Linux and Windows 11 desktops have the same security and governance controls as Windows Server desktops. These include network isolation, IAM-based access, and the compliance boundaries your organization already has in place.

To get started operating AI agents on WorkSpaces, visit: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appstream2/latest/developerguide/agent-access.html.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer prefills the email address for new threads started from cases
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer automatically fills in the customer’s email address from the linked customer profile when agents start a new email thread from a case. This saves agents time and reduces manual entry errors by eliminating the need to look up or type the address.

Cases is available in the following AWS regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation.

items.title: AWS Config now supports 10 new resource types
items.summary:
AWS Config now supports 10 additional AWS resource types across key services including Amazon ElastiCache and Amazon QuickSight. This expansion provides greater coverage over your AWS environment, enabling you to more effectively discover, assess, audit, and remediate an even broader range of resources.

With this launch, if you have enabled recording for all resource types, then AWS Config will automatically track these new additions. The newly supported resource types are also available in Config rules and Config aggregators.

You can now use AWS Config to monitor the following newly supported resource types in all AWS Regions where the resources are available:


Resource Types:

AWS::Billing::BillingView AWS::MPA::IdentitySource
AWS::Connect::HoursOfOperation AWS::Notifications::OrganizationalUnitAssociation
AWS::ElastiCache::CacheCluster AWS::NotificationsContacts::EmailContact
AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup AWS::Oam::Link
AWS::MediaLive::SignalMap AWS::QuickSight::Agent

items.title: Amazon RDS now supports the latest Cumulative Update and GDR updates for Microsoft SQL Server
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports the latest Cumulative Updates (CU) and General Distribution Release (GDR) updates for Microsoft SQL Server. This release includes support for Microsoft SQL Server 2017 CU31+GDR KB5128496 (RDS version 14.00.3560.2.v1), SQL Server 2019 CU32+GDR KB5128494 (RDS version 15.00.4500.2.v1), SQL Server 2022 CU27+GDR KB5126934 (RDS version 16.00.4305.5.v1) and SQL Server 2025 CU10 KB5125471 (RDS version 17.00.5035.5.v1).

For additional information on the improvements and fixes included in these updates, see Microsoft documentation for KB5128496, KB5128494, KB5126934 and KB5125471. We recommend that you upgrade your Amazon RDS for SQL Server instances to apply these updates using Amazon RDS Management Console, or by using the AWS SDK or CLI. You can learn more about upgrading your database instance in the Amazon RDS SQL Server User Guide for upgrading your RDS Microsoft SQL Server DB engine.

items.title: AWS Transform for mainframe improves the reimagine modernization workflow
items.summary:
AWS Transform for mainframe now discovers business functions with field-level precision and generates a new requirements coverage report in the assess and reimagine workflow. Previously, business functions that used the same table or file were grouped together, and you had to build your own traceability reporting from AWS Transform artifacts. With this launch, you can start modernizing z/OS COBOL and PL/I workloads from a more accurate catalog of business functions and verify requirements coverage before you build.

Business functions are now grouped only when they affect the same data fields. They also include screens and queues and carry clearer names and descriptions. The new requirements coverage report shows how every part of your application is accounted for in the generated requirements. Every line of source code is classified by how it was handled, every business rule links to the exact lines it came from, and every requirement is backed by the business rules that support it. You can review coverage from the full portfolio down to a single line before moving into forward engineering in Kiro and other IDEs.

These capabilities are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform for mainframe is available. For more information, see the AWS Region table. To learn more, visit AWS Transform for mainframe or see the AWS Transform for mainframe documentation.

items.title: Amazon CloudWatch now supports API keys for OpenTelemetry traces
items.summary:
Amazon CloudWatch now supports bearer token authentication, using API keys (bearer tokens), as an additional option for sending OpenTelemetry traces to the AWS X-Ray OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) traces endpoint. Any OTLP/HTTP client that can set an Authorization header, including the OpenTelemetry Collector and OpenTelemetry SDK exporters, can now authenticate with a bearer token instead of signing requests with AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4). This helps teams send traces from workloads that can't use the AWS SDK or short-term credentials, such as applications running on premises or in other clouds, CI/CD pipelines, and third-party tools that support only a static Authorization header.

SigV4 remains the recommended authentication method for sending traces to CloudWatch, and the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) SDKs continue to use SigV4 by default with no changes required. Traces sent with either method get the same CloudWatch capabilities, including Transaction Search, Amazon CloudWatch Application Signals, and Amazon CloudWatch Omni.

Bearer token authentication for traces is available in all commercial AWS Regions where the AWS X-Ray OTLP traces endpoint is available.

To learn more, see Setting up bearer token authentication for traces in the AWS X-Ray Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon EKS Capabilities now supports Argo CD Notifications
items.summary:
The Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) Capability for Argo CD now supports Argo CD Notifications, providing notifications when your applications sync, fail, or change health. You define triggers and message templates in your cluster and subscribe individual Applications with an annotation, the same way you do in upstream Argo CD.

With this launch, you can deliver notifications to 16 notification services, including Slack, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Amazon SQS, and Amazon EventBridge. The Amazon SQS and Amazon EventBridge services authenticate with your IAM Capability Role, so you can route deployment events into your own event-driven workflows without storing credentials in your cluster. For a service that requires third-party credentials such as a Slack token, you can specify an AWS Secrets Manager ARN in place of the secret and EKS will automatically use it on your behalf.

Notifications are available in all AWS Regions where the EKS Capability for Argo CD is available, at no additional charge. Standard charges apply for resources related to the services your notifications use, for example Amazon SQS or Amazon EventBridge. To learn more, visit Amazon EKS and refer to the Amazon EKS User Guide.

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports M8i and R8i instances in additional AWS Regions
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now supports M8i and R8i instances in additional AWS Regions. Both M8i and R8i instances are now available in Asia Pacific (New Zealand) and Canada West (Calgary), and R8i instances are now available in Europe (Milan, Stockholm, and Zurich) and Israel (Tel Aviv).

These instances are powered by custom Intel Xeon 6 processors, available only on AWS, delivering the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel processors in the cloud. The M8i and R8i instances offer up to 15% better price-performance, and 2.5x more memory bandwidth compared to previous generation Intel-based instances.

M8i and R8i instances are available for Amazon RDS for Oracle in Bring Your Own License model for Oracle Database Enterprise Edition (EE) and Oracle Database Standard Edition 2 (SE2). For EE, instances are available in sizes from large to 48xlarge, as well as bare metal sizes metal-48xl and metal-96xl. For SE2, instances are available in sizes from large to 4xlarge and bare metal sizes metal-48xl and metal-96xl. Refer to Amazon RDS for Oracle Pricing for available instance configurations, pricing, and region availability.

items.title: Haiku 5.5 now available on Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
A new Anthropic model is now available in the Kiro IDE and CLI for the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. With Haiku 5.5, all three Claude 5.5 models are now available in Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US).

Claude Haiku 5.5 is the fastest model in the Claude 5.5 family. It's a clear step up from Claude Haiku 4.5, built for work that runs in large volumes and needs quick responses. Developers can use it to summarize and compact long context, classify and route requests, process text in bulk, and make small, targeted edits across many files. It also works well as a review subagent that runs in parallel, while Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 take on harder planning and coding work. Haiku 5.5 uses adaptive thinking across five effort levels from low to max, with medium as the default. It's available with a 1M context window and a 0.06x credit multiplier. Requests over 100K tokens are billed at a 0.3x multiplier.

Ensure your IDE or CLI is updated to the latest version, then restart it to access the new model from the model selector. For more details, visit the GovCloud documentation, the monitoring and tracking guide, or contact your AWS account team. To learn more about Kiro, visit the Kiro product page.

items.title: Amazon RDS now supports per snapshot billing
items.summary:
Starting today, Amazon RDS supports per snapshot billing for Amazon RDS snapshots. Per snapshot billing allows you to get the cost of each individual snapshot.

Previously, RDS snapshot charges were aggregated at the database instance level on the Cost and Usage report as well as the Cost Explorer. This meant that while understanding the snapshot charges, you could only see the aggregate view at the database instance instead of drilling down to each individual snapshot. Now, you can use cost allocation tags on your snapshots to see exactly how much each snapshot costs, giving you a better understanding of your backups spend and budgets. Per snapshot billing is enabled by default on all RDS snapshots for no additional charge.

Per snapshot billing is available for all Amazon RDS engines in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, please visit our documentation.

items.title: Amazon Quick on desktop now uses your organization's existing Amazon Quick sign-in
items.summary:
For organizations that use Amazon Quick, the desktop application now signs users in with the same sign-in method the organization already uses for Quick on the web. Administrators no longer need to register an OIDC application in their identity provider or set up separate desktop sign-in before users can get started. If a user can sign in to Quick on the web, that user can sign in to the desktop application.

To turn on desktop access, an administrator adds the desktop connector once in the Amazon Quick console. Users then enter their Quick account name, choose Sign In, and finish signing in through their browser. This works for accounts that use IAM Identity Center, IAM federation, or native Amazon Quick users. If your organization wants to manage desktop sign-in separately, you can still set up a dedicated identity provider configuration with providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, or Ping Identity.

Amazon Quick on desktop is available in AWS Regions that support the full Amazon Quick feature set.

To get started, see Amazon Quick on desktop in the Amazon Quick User Guide.

items.title: AWS Managed Services（AMS）で AWS クラウドインフラのセキュリティを強化する
items.summary: セキュリティやデータ損失インシデントは、金銭的損失だけでなく社会的信用の失墜にもつながります。AWS の責任共有モデルにおいて「クラウドにおけるセキュリティ」はお客様の責任範囲ですが、IAM ガバナンス、パッチ管理、脅威検出、インシデント対応、コンプライアンス維持を大規模に実装・運用し続けることは容易ではありません。AWS Managed Services（AMS）は、GuardDuty による 24/365 の脅威監視、NIST 準拠のインシデント対応、自動パッチ適用、AWS Config を活用したコンプライアンスの可視化など、予防・検出・対応にわたるセキュリティのベストプラクティスを包括的に提供します。本記事では、AMS を活用してクラウドインフラのセキュリティ体制を強化する方法を紹介します。

items.title: Kiro Crew の Bot のご紹介
items.summary: 2026 年 11 月 5 日、Kiro Crew で Kiro の Bot の一般提供が始まりました。Bot は、エージェントによる作業を組み立てて進めるための新しい方法です。ばらばらのセッションで作業する代わりに、作業の特定の部分を受け持つエージェントを Bot として定義し、カスタマイズします。Bot はそれぞれ名前を持ち、長く動き続けます。Bot は自分のメモリを持ち、自分でセッションを動かすので、あなたがセッションを 1 つずつ追いかける必要はなくなります。Kiro Crew はもともと、あなたの仕事の進め方から学習します。Bot によって、その学習が蓄積される場所が変わります。

items.summary: Kiro Enterprise で、チーム全体の Kiro クレジットを 1 つの共有プールにまとめて使える「クレジットプーリング」が提供開始されました。パワーユーザーはライトユーザーの余剰クレジットを使えるため、無駄を減らせます。管理者は個人・グループ・プロファイルの各レベルで利用上限やしきい値アラートを設定でき、請求は AWS アカウント経由で行われます。

items.title: Amazon S3 Tables で Apache Hive テーブルから Apache Iceberg へのマネージドな移行が可能に
items.summary: Amazon S3 Tables で、AWS Glue Data Catalog に登録された Parquet 形式の Apache Hive テーブルを Apache Iceberg へマネージドに移行できるようになりました。パイプラインの構築やコンピューティングのプロビジョニングは不要で、本番ワークロードを動かしたまま移行でき、料金はコピーしたデータ分のみです。

items.title: トヨタはいかにして BasisPilot を構築したか – AWS 上の AI アシスト型 SAP 運用プラットフォーム
items.summary: Toyota Motor North America は、20 の SAP システムと 60 台以上の Amazon EC2 ホストを対象に、AI アシスト型の SAP 運用プラットフォーム BasisPilot を AWS 上に構築しました。AWS Lambda、Amazon DynamoDB、AWS Systems Manager によるサーバーレスかつフェーズベースのワークフローと、RBAC・承認ゲートの背後で動作する Amazon Bedrock のツール呼び出し型 AI アシスタントを組み合わせています。本記事では、そのアーキテクチャとガードレールの設計を解説します。パイロットでは SAP カーネルアップグレードの所要時間が約 70% 短縮されました。

items.title: AWS セキュリティハンズオン連続開催のご案内
items.summary: AWS Japan では、2026 年 11 月から、AWS のセキュリティサービスを実際に操作するオンラインハンズオンを週次で開催します。AWS Security Agent、AWS WAF、Amazon Inspector、フロンティアモデルを活用したソースコードの脆弱性対策などをテーマに、座学とハンズオンで、ご自身の組織で試すための最初の一歩までをお伝えします。本記事は、開催日程を随時更新する案内ページです。
